state:
Goal `tools-server`: `tools:server/nvs-ctl` has its proofs, and the driver's last sweep named two
more features of the group as owing, `tools:server/stopping-and-reloading-the-drain` and
`tools:server/nvs-service`. `bun nv proofs --owed --group tools:server` lists what each still owes.
Nothing is blocked.

A section passes `help` when it shows a fenced block or a table row holding code; an indented usage
block does not count (`tools/nv/proofs/roster.ts:160`). `# nvs ctl` keeps its indented usage block
and passes on the fenced `toml` and `text` transcripts under it, which is the shape for the two
sections left.

A `.nvst` case cannot name a mount (`crates/nvs-test/src/request.rs:67`), and a feature of this
chapter is credited by a `// covers:` marker above a Rust `#[test]` alone. An example or an attack
that needs a configuration key reads the `nvs.toml` in its own directory.

A refused `nvs ctl reload` now ends with `note: the running configuration is unchanged`
(`UNCHANGED` in `crates/nvs-server/src/control.rs`). The goal's context gained
`crates/nvs-server/src/control.rs` and `crates/nvs-cli/src/service.rs`; the pack did not print
either, and `crates/nvs-cli/src/ctl.rs` is still outside `context.modules`.

next.title: the dossier
next.note: One slice is one feature with all its feature proofs:

items.text: **`tools:server/stopping-and-reloading-the-drain`** — owes about, examples, help, hostile, tests. `rule:concurrency/a-drain-closes-a-connection-cleanly`. The section at `docs/reference/tools/25-server.md:283` says a `nvs ctl reload` drains, which is not checked against the rule or the binary: check it before writing the description. A program reads the drain with `Core\Server::isDraining()`, `nvs ctl status` prints `draining:` from `crates/nvs-server/src/control.rs:245`, and `crates/nvs-cli/tests/live_config.rs:617` is a program that keeps a request open, which a from-outside case needs.

**`tools:server/nvs-service`** — owes about, examples, help, hostile, tests. `rule:packaging/a-service-is-one-stored-argv` and `rule:packaging/the-installer-is-a-sink`. The section is `docs/reference/tools/25-server.md:375`; `unit` prints and stores nothing (`crates/nvs-cli/src/service.rs:593`, `crates/nvs-cli/src/service.rs:3065`), so its output is the fenced transcript and the from-outside case. `tools:cli/nvs-info` in `data/proofs/policy.json` is the precedent if no program can show or attack the command: decide that from what `install` reads, and say so in the commit.

backlog: `nvs agent find "nvs ctl"` matches nothing, as `nvs agent find "nvs serve"` does; `nvs agent find ctl` reaches `server#nvs-ctl`. `rule:testing/feature-proofs` says `find` reaches a feature under the name its user types. Owner: `docs/reference/tools/50-agents.md` and `crates/nvs-cli/src/agent.rs`.

A reload refused for a value (`E0601`, `limits.memory = "a lot"`) names the key and the file and no line, while `rule:config/a-reload-names-what-it-could-not-apply` says the offending line; a syntax error does print `file:line:column`. Owner: `nvs-config`'s diagnostics.

The queue-storage refusal already ends `so the running configuration is unchanged` (`crates/nvs-cli/src/serve.rs:1444`), so where that text is a reload's refusal the sentence is now printed twice; whether it reaches `Controlled::reload` is not checked. Owner: `crates/nvs-cli/src/serve.rs`.

`nvs ctl reload` run within the server's own two-second check of its files can print no `applied:` line for a key that check already applied; the cases in `crates/nvs-cli/tests/live_config.rs` that assert an `applied:` line right after a write depend on winning that race. Not seen failing.
